meta.notes: Post-triage: 11 reflection candidates from raw walker consolidated into single INFO — reflection lands inside Next.js __NEXT_DATA__/RSC payload as JSON-encoded string in urlParts, not an HTML sink. JSON string context prevents naive XSS; still worth CSP hardening. All 198 XHRs returned 2xx/3xx; no console errors; no PII/JWT/AKIA in storage or responses. No IDOR-shaped surface in dashboard-scoped XHRs.

findings.title: Query-string values reflected into Next.js RSC JSON payload (not an HTML sink)
findings.evidence: All 11 probed GET params (q, search, filter, project, view, tab, ref, id, name, sort, page) with canary value zzq...xx were echoed by /dashboard inside a <script> block as JSON-encoded strings under __NEXT_DATA__.urlParts. Context excerpt: `"urlParts":["","dashboard?q=zzqmt3529kvxx"]`. JSON encoding prevents breakout to HTML/JS execution context. See evidence/dashboard/reflect-*.html.
findings.recommendation: No direct action required — JSON serialisation is the defence. As defence-in-depth, ship a strict Content-Security-Policy (script-src 'self' with nonces) so that even if a future refactor moves the value into an unsafe sink, execution is blocked.
findings.chain_of_attack: Attacker crafts a link with a payload in any query parameter and shares it. Server echoes value into __NEXT_DATA__ JSON blob. Because value is inside a JSON string literal in a <script type="application/json"> context, the payload cannot escape the string quotes to reach a JS execution context — no XSS. Impact = None until/unless the code path changes.

findings.title: 4 dashboard controls produced no observable effect on click
findings.evidence: During interactive walk, 4 clickable elements produced no URL change, no XHR, no console event. See reports/2026-08-21-testforge-emha-space-dashboard/evidence/dashboard/clickables.json and per-click artefacts click-I-*.html.
findings.recommendation: Manual review: distinguish expected pure-CSS toggles (accordion open/close) from unwired handlers.
findings.chain_of_attack: No security impact demonstrated. Reliability signal only.
findings.retest: Manual click of each labelled control in the browser.

findings.title: Dashboard XHR surface is clean (198/198 successful, no PII/secret leaks, no IDOR-shaped ids)
findings.evidence: 198 XHR/fetch calls observed across 20 dashboard interactions. All returned 200 (197) or 303 (1). Unique endpoints: 19. Numeric/UUID id in path: 0. JWT/AKIA/private-key patterns in bodies: 0. Foreign emails: 0. See reports/2026-08-21-testforge-emha-space-dashboard/evidence/dashboard/xhrs.json.
findings.recommendation: Baseline is healthy. Re-run after any new dashboard widget lands.

findings.title: Browser storage on /dashboard contains no tokens, PII, or secret-shaped values
findings.evidence: localStorage + sessionStorage snapshot after login. No JWT, no AWS key, no private key, no `password:` field, no key names matching /session_id|api_key|refresh_token|access_token/. See reports/2026-08-21-testforge-emha-space-dashboard/evidence/dashboard/storage.json.
findings.recommendation: Continue keeping session material in HttpOnly cookies (as observed).
findings.retest: Open devtools > Application > Storage on /dashboard while authenticated.

findings.title: Zero JS console errors and zero unhandled promise rejections during dashboard walk
findings.recommendation: Good hygiene — keep an eye when adding new widgets.
findings.retest: Re-run node scripts/dashboard-deep-walk.js after new features land.
